1.modern-en: Ivan Ilyich appears only as a corpse: his death notice is read aloud to his colleagues, and his body lies in the death chamber while Peter Ivanovich pays his respects. His waxen face wears an expression that seems both finished and reproachful. We learn he was a Member of the Court of Justice, fond of bridge, and that he screamed in agony for three days before he died.
1.modern-da: Ivan Ilyich optræder kun som lig: hans dødsannonce læses højt for kollegerne, og hans krop ligger i dødskammeret, mens Peter Ivanovich viser sin respekt. Hans voksgule ansigt bærer et udtryk, der både virker fuldbyrdet og bebrejdende. Vi får at vide, at han var medlem af justitsretten, glad for whist, og at han skreg af smerte i tre dage, før han døde.

2.modern-en: His ordinary, decorous rise is traced from boyhood. The bright "phoenix of the family," he finishes the School of Law, takes a provincial post, and learns early to live for propriety and the approval of people of rank. He marries Praskovya Fyodorovna almost by default, and when she turns difficult in pregnancy, he retreats into his official work as a refuge.
2.modern-da: Hans almindelige, sømmelige stigning følges fra drengeår. Den kvikke »familiens føniks« gennemfører retsskolen, tager en provinspost og lærer tidligt at leve for sømmelighed og de fornemmes anerkendelse. Han gifter sig med Praskovya Fyodorovna nærmest pr. automatik, og da hun bliver vanskelig under graviditeten, trækker han sig ind i sit embedsarbejde som tilflugt.

3.modern-en: After a bitter year being passed over, Ivan Ilyich gambles on a trip to Petersburg and lands a coveted post with a five-thousand-ruble salary. Restored to good spirits, he throws himself into furnishing a fine new house exactly to his taste. On a step-ladder hanging curtains he slips and bangs his side against a window knob, a bruise he soon forgets.
3.modern-da: Efter et bittert år med at blive forbigået satser Ivan Ilyich på en rejse til Petersborg og lander en eftertragtet post med en løn på fem tusind rubler. Med humøret genrejst kaster han sig over at indrette et fint nyt hus helt efter sin smag. På en trappestige, mens han hænger gardiner op, glider han og slår sin side mod et vindueshåndtag, et blåt mærke han hurtigt glemmer.

4.modern-en: A strange taste and a pressure in his side harden into a constant ache, and his temper sours the whole household. A celebrated doctor examines him with the same lofty evasion Ivan Ilyich himself uses on defendants, and refuses to say whether the case is dangerous. He sinks into dread, consulting more doctors and medical books, and even at the bridge table the gnawing pain now intrudes.
4.modern-da: En underlig smag og et tryk i siden hærder til en konstant smerte, og hans humør forgifter hele husstanden. En berømt læge undersøger ham med den samme ophøjede undvigelse, som Ivan Ilyich selv bruger over for anklagede, og nægter at sige, om sygdommen er farlig. Han synker ned i rædsel, opsøger flere læger og lægebøger, og selv ved whistbordet trænger den nagende smerte sig nu ind.

5.modern-en: His brother-in-law's shocked stare tells him how wasted he has become, and he overhears his wife told that he is "as good as dead." He clings to the doctors' talk of a curable appendix, and for an evening half-believes it. Then, alone in bed, the truth breaks through: it is not a question of the appendix or the kidney but of life and death, and he is dying.
5.modern-da: Hans svogers forskrækkede blik fortæller ham, hvor udtæret han er blevet, og han hører sin kone få at vide, at han er »så godt som død«. Han klynger sig til lægernes tale om en helbredelig blindtarm og halvt tror på det en aften. Så, alene i sengen, bryder sandheden igennem: det handler ikke om blindtarmen eller nyren, men om liv og død, og han er ved at dø.

6.modern-en: Ivan Ilyich cannot make his own death real to himself: the textbook syllogism "Caius is mortal" was never meant for little Vanya, with all his particular memories and loves. He hunts for old screens to hide the thought, throwing himself back into court work, but the pain and the awareness of It break through every distraction. He is left to look It in the face and suffer, able to do nothing.
6.modern-da: Ivan Ilyich kan ikke gøre sin egen død virkelig for sig selv: lærebogens syllogisme »Cajus er dødelig« var aldrig ment for lille Vanja med alle hans særlige minder og kærligheder. Han søger gamle skærme til at skjule tanken bag, kaster sig tilbage i retsarbejdet, men smerten og bevidstheden om Det bryder igennem enhver adspredelse. Han efterlades med at se Det i øjnene og lide, ude af stand til at gøre noget.

7.modern-en: Now bedridden and tended in his most degrading needs, Ivan Ilyich finds his only comfort in the peasant Gerasim, who holds his legs up for hours without complaint. What torments him most is the universal lie that he is merely ill, not dying, in which everyone but Gerasim insists he take part. He longs, secretly and shamefully, to be pitied and wept over like a sick child.
7.modern-da: Nu sengeliggende og passet i sine mest ydmygende behov finder Ivan Ilyich sin eneste trøst i bonden Gerasim, som holder hans ben oppe i timevis uden at klage. Det, der piner ham mest, er den almindelige løgn om, at han blot er syg og ikke døende, en løgn alle på nær Gerasim insisterer på, at han deltager i. Han længes, hemmeligt og skamfuldt, efter at blive ynket og grædt over som et sygt barn.

8.modern-en: A single day unfolds in its sameness: tea he cannot stomach, the footman Peter, the cheerful doctor's hollow ritual, his wife's rustling hatefulness. A famous specialist taps and consults and offers only a vague "possibility" of recovery. That evening the family dresses for the theater, and Ivan Ilyich, after insisting they go, is left alone with his pain when they leave.
8.modern-da: En enkelt dag udfolder sig i sin ensformighed: te, han ikke kan holde nede, tjeneren Peter, den muntre læges hule ritual, konens raslende afskyelighed. En berømt specialist banker og rådfører sig og tilbyder kun en vag »mulighed« for helbredelse. Den aften klæder familien sig på til teatret, og Ivan Ilyich, efter selv at have insisteret på at de skal af sted, efterlades alene med sin smerte, da de går.

9.modern-en: After a night sinking into a black sack from which he cannot fall through, Ivan Ilyich sends Gerasim away and weeps like a child over his loneliness and the silence of God. An inner voice asks what he wants; reviewing his life, he finds that only childhood holds anything truly good, while everything since has thinned into the petty and repugnant. A thought surfaces and is at once dismissed: perhaps he did not live as he should have.
9.modern-da: Efter en nat, hvor han synker ned i en sort sæk, han ikke kan falde igennem, sender Ivan Ilyich Gerasim bort og græder som et barn over sin ensomhed og Guds tavshed. En indre stemme spørger, hvad han vil; idet han ser sit liv efter, finder han, at kun barndommen rummer noget virkelig godt, mens alt siden er tyndet ud i det smålige og frastødende. En tanke dukker op og afvises straks: måske levede han ikke, som han burde.

10.modern-en: For two more weeks he lies on the sofa facing the wall, swinging between dread of an incomprehensible death and faint hope in his failing body. He lives almost entirely in memories that always travel back to childhood, where alone there was real life. He pictures his life as a stone falling, gathering speed toward the final agony, and finds no answer to the question of what it has all been for.
10.modern-da: I to uger mere ligger han på sofaen med ansigtet mod væggen og svinger mellem rædsel for en ufattelig død og et svagt håb til sin svigtende krop. Han lever næsten helt i minder, der altid rejser tilbage til barndommen, hvor der alene var virkeligt liv. Han forestiller sig sit liv som en sten, der falder og tager fart mod den sidste dødskval, og finder intet svar på, hvad det hele har været til for.

11.modern-en: Looking at Gerasim's kindly face, the question strikes him with full force: "What if my whole life has been wrong?" He begins to suspect that everything he built and defended was a vast fraud, and the realization multiplies his physical agony. To please his weeping wife he takes communion, briefly hoping again to live; but when she says he looks better, his hatred and the pain come surging back, and he shouts at her to go away.
11.modern-da: Mens han ser på Gerasims venlige ansigt, rammer spørgsmålet ham med fuld kraft: »Hvad nu, hvis hele mit liv har været forkert?« Han begynder at ane, at alt, hvad han byggede og forsvarede, var ét stort bedrag, og erkendelsen mangedobler hans fysiske kval. For at føje sin grædende kone modtager han nadveren og håber et øjeblik atter at leve; men da hun siger, han ser bedre ud, vælder hadet og smerten tilbage, og han råber, at hun skal gå.

12.modern-en: Ivan Ilyich screams for three days, held back from death by his clinging conviction that his life was good. When his son catches his hand and kisses it, pity breaks through; he sees that he is making his family suffer and that he must act to free them. In that instant the fear of death dissolves into light, and he dies whispering that death itself is finished.
12.modern-da: Ivan Ilyich skriger i tre dage, holdt tilbage fra døden af sin fastholdte overbevisning om, at hans liv var godt. Da hans søn griber hans hånd og kysser den, bryder medlidenheden igennem; han ser, at han gør sin familie ondt, og at han må handle for at sætte dem fri. I det øjeblik opløses dødsangsten i lys, og han dør, mens han hvisker, at selve døden er forbi.

1.modern-en: As the new widow she receives Peter Ivanovich in black lace, pressing his hand and inviting his sympathy. Yet her real purpose, beneath the tears, is practical: she has already worked out the cost of the grave and wants advice on squeezing more money out of the government pension. Her grief and her bookkeeping run side by side.
1.modern-da: Som den nye enke modtager hun Peter Ivanovich i sort blonde, trykker hans hånd og indbyder til medfølelse. Men hendes egentlige ærinde, under tårerne, er praktisk: hun har allerede regnet gravstedets pris ud og vil have råd om at presse flere penge ud af statspensionen. Hendes sorg og hendes regnskab løber side om side.

2.modern-en: The clever, attractive girl of good family wins Ivan Ilyich on the dance floor, and he marries her almost without deciding to. But from the first months of pregnancy she turns jealous, demanding, and prone to coarse scenes, disturbing the easy life he prizes. Their marriage settles into a war he answers by retreating into his work.
2.modern-da: Den kloge, tiltrækkende pige af god familie vinder Ivan Ilyich på dansegulvet, og han gifter sig med hende nærmest uden at beslutte det. Men fra de første måneder af graviditeten bliver hun jaloux, krævende og tilbøjelig til grove scener og forstyrrer det lette liv, han sætter pris på. Deres ægteskab sætter sig i en krig, han besvarer ved at trække sig ind i sit arbejde.

3.modern-en: When Ivan Ilyich returns triumphant from Petersburg, Praskovya Fyodorovna brightens and the two share a rare truce, her plans for the new town aligning neatly with his. Settled into the fine house, they get on better than in years, though a furious quarrel still erupts over cakes and the confectioner's bill at their dance.
3.modern-da: Da Ivan Ilyich vender triumferende hjem fra Petersborg, kvikker Praskovya Fyodorovna op, og de to deler en sjælden våbenhvile, hvor hendes planer for den nye by passer pænt med hans. Veletablerede i det fine hus kommer de bedre ud af det med hinanden end i årevis, selv om et rasende skænderi alligevel bryder ud over kager og konditorens regning ved deres bal.

4.modern-en: As his irritability grows, she at first fights back, then concludes his temper is simply dreadful and pities herself for enduring it. She insists he see the famous doctor and adopts a fixed line for her friends: that Ivan Ilyich brings his illness on himself by not following the treatment. Her buried wish that he would die feeds his own bitterness.
4.modern-da: Efterhånden som hans irritabilitet vokser, slår hun først igen, men konkluderer så, at hans humør simpelthen er forfærdeligt, og ynker sig selv for at udholde det. Hun insisterer på, at han ser den berømte læge, og lægger en fast linje over for sine veninder: at Ivan Ilyich selv påfører sig sygdommen ved ikke at følge behandlingen. Hendes begravede ønske om, at han skulle dø, nærer hans egen bitterhed.

5.modern-en: Overheard arguing with her brother that Ivan Ilyich is "as good as dead," she nonetheless plays the gentle, worried wife to his face, a gentleness that only irritates him. She proposes calling in the famous specialist no matter the cost, and kisses his forehead goodnight while he hates her with all his soul.
5.modern-da: Overhørt mens hun skændes med sin bror om, at Ivan Ilyich er »så godt som død«, spiller hun ikke desto mindre den blide, bekymrede hustru over for ham, en blidhed der kun irriterer ham. Hun foreslår at tilkalde den berømte specialist uanset prisen og kysser ham på panden til godnat, mens han hader hende af hele sin sjæl.

8.modern-en: She sweeps in during the doctor's visit, scolding the footman and proving she has been up for hours. To her husband she keeps her fixed reproach, that he won't follow orders and lies with his legs up, and arranges for a celebrated specialist as a thing she claims to do "for herself." That evening she dresses for the theater, and her powdered, corseted health fills him with hatred.
8.modern-da: Hun fejer ind under lægens besøg, skænder på tjeneren og beviser, at hun har været oppe i timevis. Over for sin mand fastholder hun sin faste bebrejdelse, at han ikke vil følge ordrer og ligger med benene oppe, og arrangerer en berømt specialist som noget, hun påstår at gøre »for sin egen skyld«. Den aften klæder hun sig på til teatret, og hendes pudrede, snørede sundhed fylder ham med had.

9.modern-en: Coming home late from the theater, she creeps in on tiptoe and offers to send Gerasim away and sit up with him herself, but he refuses her. She presses opium on him and, when he gives in and takes it, leaves him to the night.
9.modern-da: Hun kommer sent hjem fra teatret, lister ind på tæerne og tilbyder at sende Gerasim bort og selv våge hos ham, men han afviser hende. Hun presser opium på ham, og da han giver efter og tager det, overlader hun ham til natten.

11.modern-en: She comes meaning to share the news of Petrishchev's proposal but finds him worse and looking at her with naked hatred. Later she begs him, weeping, to take communion, framing it as harmless and helpful, and he gives in to please her. When she congratulates him afterward and asks if he feels better, her whole presence tells him the lie of his life, and he screams at her to leave.
11.modern-da: Hun kommer for at dele nyheden om Petrishchevs frieri, men finder ham værre og med et blik fyldt af nøgent had mod hende. Senere bønfalder hun ham grædende om at modtage nadveren, fremstiller det som harmløst og hjælpsomt, og han giver efter for at føje hende. Da hun bagefter lykønsker ham og spørger, om han har det bedre, fortæller hele hendes nærvær ham løgnen i hans liv, og han skriger til hende, at hun skal gå.

12.modern-en: In the final hours she comes to his bedside, mouth open and face streaked with tears of despair. Looking at her, Ivan Ilyich is filled with pity rather than hatred, and tries to ask her forgiveness before he dies.
12.modern-da: I de sidste timer kommer hun hen til hans seng med åben mund og et ansigt stribet af fortvivlelsens tårer. Da Ivan Ilyich ser på hende, fyldes han af medlidenhed frem for had og forsøger at bede hende om tilgivelse, før han dør.

1.modern-en: The butler's young assistant moves lightly through the funeral, scattering something on the floor against the smell of decay. He had served as Ivan Ilyich's sick-nurse, whom the dead man was very fond of. Helping Peter Ivanovich into his coat, he says simply, "It's God's will. We'll all come to it in the end."
1.modern-da: Hovmesterens unge medhjælper bevæger sig let gennem begravelsen og strør noget på gulvet mod forrådnelsens lugt. Han havde tjent som Ivan Ilyichs sygeplejer, som den afdøde holdt meget af. Mens han hjælper Peter Ivanovich i frakken, siger han enkelt: »Det er Guds vilje. Vi ender alle dér til sidst.«

4.modern-en: He is named only in passing, as the servant Praskovya Fyodorovna will send to the chemist's with the prescription.
4.modern-da: Han nævnes kun i forbifarten, som tjeneren Praskovya Fyodorovna vil sende til apoteket med recepten.

7.modern-en: The clean, healthy young peasant takes on the most degrading care of the dying man without a trace of disgust, and becomes Ivan Ilyich's one comfort. He holds his master's legs up for hours, even all night, refusing to go to bed. Alone among them he does not lie, telling Ivan Ilyich plainly, "We're all going to die, so why should I begrudge a little trouble?"
7.modern-da: Den rene, sunde unge bonde påtager sig den mest ydmygende pleje af den døende mand uden et spor af afsky og bliver Ivan Ilyichs eneste trøst. Han holder sin herres ben oppe i timevis, endda hele natten, og nægter at gå i seng. Som den eneste blandt dem lyver han ikke, men siger ligeud til Ivan Ilyich: »Vi skal alle dø, så hvorfor skulle jeg fortryde en lille ulejlighed?«

9.modern-en: Gerasim sits dozing in quiet patience at the foot of the bed, the dying man's legs propped on his shoulders. When Ivan Ilyich tells him to go, he answers it is no trouble and offers to stay longer, and only leaves when ordered, letting his master weep alone.
9.modern-da: Gerasim sidder og blunder i stille tålmodighed for fodenden af sengen med den døende mands ben hvilende på sine skuldre. Da Ivan Ilyich beder ham gå, svarer han, at det ingen ulejlighed er, og tilbyder at blive længere, og går først, da han får ordre til det, og lader sin herre græde alene.

11.modern-en: It is the sight of Gerasim's sleepy, kindly, high-cheekboned face in the night that triggers the question that undoes Ivan Ilyich: "What if my whole life has been wrong?"
11.modern-da: Det er synet af Gerasims søvnige, venlige ansigt med de høje kindben om natten, der udløser spørgsmålet, som vælter Ivan Ilyich: »Hvad nu, hvis hele mit liv har været forkert?«

1.modern-en: Ivan Ilyich's closest acquaintance and old schoolfellow, Peter Ivanovich brings the news of his death and goes to the house to pay his respects. There he fumbles through the rituals of crossing himself and condolence, manages the rebellious springs of an ottoman, and listens to the widow's pension troubles. The sight of the corpse stirs a brief terror for himself, quickly soothed, and he leaves to take a hand at bridge after all.
1.modern-da: Ivan Ilyichs nærmeste bekendt og gamle skolekammerat, Peter Ivanovich, bringer nyheden om hans død og tager hjem til huset for at vise sin respekt. Der famler han sig gennem korsets tegn og kondolencens ritualer, kæmper med en genstridig puf og hører på enkens pensionsbekymringer. Synet af liget vækker en kort rædsel for ham selv, hurtigt beroliget, og han går for alligevel at få en tørn whist.

1.modern-en: At the funeral Schwartz, lean and elegant with his Piccadilly side-whiskers, wears a look of mock gravity that cannot hide his real playfulness. With winks and the bridge cards in mind, he embodies the unshaken routine of pleasure that death is not allowed to interrupt. His untroubled face is a comfort to Peter Ivanovich, signaling that none of this need spoil their evening.
1.modern-da: Ved begravelsen bærer Schwartz, slank og elegant med sine Piccadilly-bakkenbarter, et udtryk af spillet alvor, der ikke kan skjule hans virkelige munterhed. Med blinkene og whistkortene i tankerne legemliggør han den urokkelige nydelsesrutine, som døden ikke får lov at afbryde. Hans ubekymrede ansigt er en trøst for Peter Ivanovich og signalerer, at intet af dette behøver ødelægge deres aften.

4.modern-en: Now seen through the eyes of the dying man, Schwartz especially gets on Ivan Ilyich's nerves with his jokiness, liveliness, and savoir-faire, all of which remind Ivan Ilyich painfully of what he himself had been ten years before.
4.modern-da: Nu set gennem den døende mands øjne går Schwartz især Ivan Ilyich på nerverne med sin spøgefuldhed, sin livlighed og sin savoir-faire, alt sammen noget der smerteligt minder Ivan Ilyich om, hvad han selv havde været ti år tidligere.

4.modern-en: The celebrated doctor examines Ivan Ilyich with exactly the lofty, evasive air Ivan Ilyich himself uses on defendants, weighing a floating kidney against the appendix while refusing the one question that matters: is it dangerous? A string of further doctors and a homeopath each diagnose differently, deepening his confusion and dread. Their indifference to a matter of life and death wounds him.
4.modern-da: Den berømte læge undersøger Ivan Ilyich med præcis den ophøjede, undvigende mine, Ivan Ilyich selv bruger over for anklagede, og vejer en vandrende nyre mod blindtarmen, mens han afviser det ene spørgsmål, der betyder noget: er det farligt? En række yderligere læger og en homøopat stiller hver sin diagnose og uddyber hans forvirring og rædsel. Deres ligegyldighed over for et spørgsmål om liv og død sårer ham.

5.modern-en: Peter Ivanovich's doctor friend goes over the anatomy with Ivan Ilyich and persuades him, for a while, that a small thing in the appendix could be set right. The hope holds through dinner and the evening, until the old pain returns in bed and shatters it.
5.modern-da: Peter Ivanovichs lægeven gennemgår anatomien med Ivan Ilyich og overbeviser ham for en stund om, at en lille ting i blindtarmen kunne bringes i orden. Håbet holder gennem middagen og aftenen, indtil den gamle smerte vender tilbage i sengen og knuser det.

8.modern-en: The fresh, plump, cheerful doctor arrives wearing a reassuring expression he can no longer take off, rubbing his hands and putting his patient through the familiar tapping and listening that Ivan Ilyich knows to be pure deception. A famous specialist follows with the same weighty talk of kidney and appendix, and at the timid question of recovery offers only a vague "possibility."
8.modern-da: Den friske, buttede, muntre læge ankommer med et beroligende udtryk, han ikke længere kan tage af, gnider sine hænder og udsætter sin patient for den velkendte banken og lytten, som Ivan Ilyich ved er rent bedrag. En berømt specialist følger efter med den samme tungtvejende tale om nyre og blindtarm, og på det forsigtige spørgsmål om helbredelse tilbyder han kun en vag »mulighed«.

11.modern-en: Coming at his usual hour, the doctor meets only "Yes" and "No" and Ivan Ilyich's angry eyes, and is told he can do nothing and should leave. He admits to Praskovya Fyodorovna in the drawing room that the case is very grave, and that nothing remains but opium to dull the unbearable suffering.
11.modern-da: Da lægen kommer på sin sædvanlige time, mødes han kun af »ja« og »nej« og Ivan Ilyichs vrede øjne og får at vide, at han intet kan gøre og bør gå. I dagligstuen indrømmer han over for Praskovya Fyodorovna, at sygdommen er meget alvorlig, og at der intet er tilbage andet end opium til at dæmpe den uudholdelige lidelse.
